rules.title: Security deposit capped at 1.5 months' rent; annual increases capped at 10%
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit. Prepaid rent, including last month's rent and pet deposits, counts toward the cap.
rules.key_value: 1.5x monthly rent; yearly increase max 10% of current deposit
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties in New Jersey, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant sends a written request to the landlord to comply, effective 30 days later.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupied 2-3 family dwelling exemption can be waived by tenant written request

rules.penalty: Unlawful use of security deposit monies: disorderly person, fine of not less than $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment, or both (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).

rules.title: Return of security deposit within 30 days with itemized deductions
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy terminates, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions sent by personal delivery or registered or certified mail. A tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and attorney's fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies subject to the Security Deposit Law.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in by written request.

rules.title: Security deposit held in trust in interest-bearing NJ account; interest belongs to tenant
rules.requirement: Deposits must be held in trust in an insured New Jersey interest-bearing account or a qualifying money market fund. Within 30 days of receipt, and annually, the landlord must notify the tenant in writing of the institution, amount, account type and interest rate. Interest belongs to the tenant and is paid annually in cash or as a rent credit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords receiving security deposits. Investment options differ for landlords holding deposits for 10 or more units.
rules.exemptions: Seasonal use or rental of 125 consecutive days or less, for this section. Owner-occupied 2-3 family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.penalty: If proper notice or interest is not given, the tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% annual interest toward rent (N.J.S.A. 46:8-19.1(c)).

rules.title: Deposit return within 5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation
rules.requirement: The landlord must return the security deposit within five business days after a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation. This applies where a public official has posted a notice prohibiting occupancy or certified that the displacement will last more than seven days.

rules.title: Deposit return within 15 business days after domestic-violence lease termination
rules.requirement: When a tenant terminates a lease under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the deposit plus interest available within 15 business days. The landlord must also notify the tenant within 3 business days of where and when it can be picked up.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants who terminate a lease as domestic violence victims under the Safe Housing Act.

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act good-cause requirement
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease, written or oral, without one of the statutory good causes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)-(r)). Notice to Cease and Notice to Quit requirements apply depending on the cause.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including single-family homes, mobile homes and mobile home park land, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or three units and no more than two rental units. Hotel, motel or guest house transient or seasonal guests, unless the occupant has no alternate residence and lives there continually. Units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner occupancy of 2-3 unit buildings; transient/seasonal status

rules.penalty: Treble damages plus attorney fees and costs for owner-occupancy or removal-from-market violations, and civil penalty up to $10,000 per violation (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.6).

rules.title: Relocation assistance of six months' rent for illegal-occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted to correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the monthly rent, paid by the landlord. If unpaid, the municipal fund may pay, or 18% annual interest accrues and the amount becomes a lien.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted under the illegal occupancy ground of the Anti-Eviction Act.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Eviction must be for illegal occupancy

rules.penalty: 18% annual interest on unpaid balance; lien on property (N.J.A.C. 5:11-8.5(c)).

rules.title: Owner move-in eviction requires six months of personal occupancy
rules.requirement: After evicting for personal occupancy, the landlord must personally occupy the unit for at least six months. Re-renting or converting instead makes the landlord liable for treble damages plus fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units vacated after an owner personal-occupancy notice.
rules.penalty: Three times damages plus attorney fees and costs.

rules.title: Rent increases may not be unconscionable; no mid-lease increases
rules.requirement: A landlord may not raise rent mid-lease and must terminate the lease with proper notice to quit and notice of increase. A tenant cannot be evicted for nonpayment of an increase that is unconscionable or that violates municipal rent control.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Same as the Anti-Eviction Act, e.g., owner-occupied 2-3 unit premises.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Unconscionability is fact-sensitive and determined by a court

rules.quoted_span: A landlord cannot raise the rent mid-lease term.
rules.conflict_note: Municipal rent control ordinances, where they exist, apply in addition to this standard.

rules.title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years
rules.requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinance for 30 years after construction is completed. Government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, within 30 years after completion of construction.

rules.conflict_note: This is a state preemption of local rent control for new buildings rather than a cap.

rules.title: No rent increases to cover condominium/cooperative conversion costs
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, rents may not be raised to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion. Increases for new services or amenities are still allowed.
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenants in buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership.

rules.title: Law Against Discrimination: protected classes including source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or otherwise discriminate based on protected characteristics. These include race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, familial status, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, nationality, and source of lawful income.
